public_text.3:
High affinity, somatically mutated anti-OVA Ig is a T-dependent germinal centre / T follicular helper product.

* AID –V18R G1.  AID catalytic activity is required for deamination in IgV and for affinity maturation in the GC. A catalytically dead / SHM-deficient AID allele abolishes the generation of SHM + high-affinity OVA Ig.
* CD40-KO G2. CD40–CD40L signalling on the B cell is obligatory for Tfh licensing, germinal centre formation, AID up-regulation and affinity maturation. No CD40 = no T-dependent GC SHM.
* I-Ad peptide presentation. In BALB/c the immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope is I-Ad restricted. 

  G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A is a β1 groove mutant that essentially abolishes peptide binding/loading by I-Ad. No OVA peptide can be presented to OVA-specific CD4+ T cells, no OVA-specific Tfh help is generated and the OVA-specific GC/SHM response is lost.
  G5 H2-IAd-T139A is the classic I-Ad β1 mutant that selectively destroys the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex recognition by OVA-specific CD4+ T cells. G2 CD40-KO: obligatory for Tfh help, GC formation, AID up-regulation, class-switch and affinity maturation. No T-dependent GC/SHM. Unanimous loss.

G4 CD8-V247D: MHC-I co-receptor defect; CD4 Tfh help/GC/SHM to a soluble protein is unaffected. Unanimous wild-type-like.

G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A: E137/V142 are floor residues of I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. Most colleagues in this round score this quantitative adjuvant-dependent reduction as “significantly different titre”. Some score it only as a quantitative adjuvant effect and retain SHM competence per se.

Weight of evidence for the question as phrased – titre after repeated OVA+CpG – is loss in G1, G2, G3 and G6, with G4 unchanged and G5 essentially WT-like under the CD4-contact interpretation. That is the G1,G2,G3,G6 set, option B.

Alternative readings that remain in the discussion: 
* strict SHM competence only → MyD88 removed → core AID/CD40/peptide presentation: G1,G2,G3,G5, option D;
* T139A read as peptide-presentation null and MyD88 scored as titre reduction → G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, option C.

Unresolved points: precise functional classification of I-Ad T139A for OVA323-339 presentation vs CD4 binding, and whether CpG-adjuvant magnitude reduction in MyD88-KO is counted as a mechanistic loss of SHM-derived high-affinity titre. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core T-dependent GC/SHM requirements are stable across rounds.

* G4 CD8-V247D affects MHC-I/CD8 co-receptor. CD8+ CTL function is dispensable for CD4 Tfh-driven GC SHM of a protein antigen → WT-like.

MHC-II I-Ad mutants:

* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A is a peptide-binding groove floor mutation in I-Ad β1 that abrogates peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and abolishes presentation of the immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. OVA-specific Tfh help, GC and SHM are lost. Consensus.
* G5 H2-IAd-T139A is contested. Mechanistic view supported by majority in this round: T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helix at the CD4 co-receptor binding surface, not the peptide floor. T139A impairs CD4–MHC II interaction but leaves peptide binding and TCR recognition of the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex largely intact. Under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG immunisation CD4 co-receptor function can be compensated and OVA-specific Tfh priming/GC SHM remains essentially WT-like. Alternative view held by a minority: T139A is read as destroying the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex and abrogating OVA-specific CD4 priming, so OVA-specific GC/SHM is lost. If that interpretation is taken, G5 behaves like G3.

MyD88:

* G6 MyD88-KO removes TLR9–MyD88 signalling by the CpG adjuvant. CpG drives DC maturation, type I IFN and TLR9 signalling in B cells that amplify the T-dependent GC response to OVA+CpG.
* One camp scores this as a marked quantitative reduction in GC magnitude and therefore a significantly lower titer of high-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig under the OVA+CpG repeated immunisation protocol → G6 different.
* The other camp argues T-dependent GC formation and AID-mediated SHM per se can still occur to protein antigen in the absence of MyD88-dependent TLR signalling; loss is adjuvant magnitude not loss of SHM competence.

Current distribution in round 1:
B. G1,G2,G3,G6 is argued by Colleagues 1,2,4,7,8 with G5 scored WT-like and MyD88 scored as titer-reducing.
C. G1,G2,G3,G5,G6 is argued by Colleagues 3,5,6 with G5 scored as OVA-specific peptide presentation loss and MyD88 scored as titer-reducing.

Unresolved points: precise classification of T139A in I-Ad as CD4-contact vs peptide-presenting mutant in BALB/c; whether the question intends “significantly different titer” to include quantitative adjuvant amplification via MyD88 or only loss of SHM competence.

Best synthesis retained: AID-V18R, CD40-KO and I-Ad peptide-groove E137A/V142A are unambiguously different; CD8-V247D is a true negative control; T139A is most plausibly a CD4-binding defect compensated under strong repeated immunisation → WT-like; MyD88-KO reduces CpG-adjuvanted magnitude → significantly different titer under the protocol as written. 2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The high-affinity OVA-specific Ig that is SHM-derived is a T-dependent GC / Tfh output. Non-negotiable requirements are enzymatically competent AID in B cells, CD40–CD40L licensing of B cells for GC entry/AID induction, and cognate OVA peptide : I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CpG ODN adjuvant signals through TLR9–MyD88 and amplifies the magnitude of the T-dependent GC response under the repeated OVA+CpG protocol.

G1 AID-V18R
AID V18R is catalytically dead / SHM-deficient. No V-region deamination, no GC affinity maturation. High-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig is essentially absent. Different from WT. Uncontested.

G2 CD40-KO
CD40 signalling on B cells is obligatory for Tfh help, GC formation, AID up-regulation, class switch and maintenance of the SHM programme. No T-dependent GC → no SHM-derived high-affinity OVA Ig. Different from WT. Uncontested.

G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A
E137/V142 are floor residues of the I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. E137A/V142A abolishes peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and specifically abrogates presentation of the immunodominant BALB/c OVA323-339 epitope to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. Loss of OVA-specific Tfh help → loss of OVA-specific GC and SHM. Different from WT. Uncontested.

G4 CD8-V247D
CD8 is an MHC-I co-receptor. CD8+ CTL function is dispensable for CD4 Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM of a soluble protein T-dependent response. OVA-specific high-affinity SHM Ig titer is essentially WT-like. Uncontested.

G5 H2-IAd-T139A
Disputed mechanistic reading. 
* Peptide-presentation loss reading: T139 lies in the I-Ad β1 helical face contacting the OVA323-339/I-Ad complex; T139A selectively destroys binding/presentation/recognition of the immunodominant OVA peptide by I-Ad while preserving general MHC II expression. OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help is lost → OVA-specific GC/SHM lost. This gives G5 different from WT, as in options C/D.
* CD4-co-receptor contact reading: T139A is the classic I-Ad CD4-binding surface mutant. Peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained; CD4 co-receptor engagement is impaired but dispensable for peripheral T-dependent help under high antigen load and repeated boosting with OVA+CpG. Tfh differentiation and GC SHM to OVA are essentially preserved, so the high-affinity SHM OVA titer is not significantly altered. This gives G5 WT-like, as in options B.
The current round is split ~5 vs 3 on this reading, with the CD4-binding compensated view prevailing among the B-supporters.

G6 MyD88-KO
CpG ODN signals exclusively via TLR9→MyD88 in DCs/B cells. MyD88 deficiency removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated B cell licensing, blunting the adjuvant amplification of the T-dependent GC response. 
* Quantitative titer reading: With repeated OVA+CpG immunisation the magnitude of GC formation and the measurable titer of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced relative to WT+CpG, so the titer is significantly different. This supports inclusion of G6, options B/C.
* Qualitative SHM competence reading: SHM per se can still be generated to protein antigen in the absence of MyD88-dependent TLR signalling; the loss is adjuvant-driven magnitude, not a loss of SHM competence. Under a strict SHM-competence read-out MyD88-KO is not scored as a loss, supporting exclusion of G6, options D and the G1,G2,G3,G5 core.

Consensus core non-negotiable defects: G1, G2, G3. G4 is a true negative control.

Unresolved tension:
* Whether T139A is scored as an OVA-specific peptide-presentation null, G5 different, or a CD4-contact mutant compensated by repeated high-dose OVA+CpG, G5 WT-like.
* Whether a CpG-adjuvant magnitude reduction in MyD88-KO counts as “significantly different” titer of SHM-derived high-affinity antibody, or whether only the qualitative SHM machinery is scored.

The majority current-round positions cluster on B = G1,G2,G3,G6 with CD8-WT and T139A WT-like under repeated boosting, with a sizeable minority on C = G1,G2,G3,G5,G6 and the classical core D = G1,G2,G3,G5 when MyD88 is treated as a quantitative adjuvant effect only.

G4 CD8-V247D: MHC-I co-receptor defect; CD4 Tfh help/GC/SHM to a soluble protein is unaffected. Unanimous wild-type-like.

G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A: E137/V142 are floor residues of I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. Abrogates peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and specifically abolishes presentation of the immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope in BALB/c. No OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help → no OVA-specific GC/SHM. Unanimous loss.

G5 H2-IAd-T139A: contested interpretation. The current round majority treats T139A as the classic I-Ad β1 CD4 co-receptor contact mutant: peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained, CD4 engagement is impaired but dispensable under high antigen load/repeated OVA+CpG boosting, so OVA-specific Tfh help and GC SHM are essentially preserved, WT-like. A minority treats T139A as selective loss of OVA323-339 presentation/recognition, i.e. an OVA-specific CD4 help defect analogous to G3. Evidence for the CD4-contact interpretation is stronger in the literature; E137A/V142A is the peptide-groove null.

G6 MyD88-KO: CpG signals exclusively via TLR9-MyD88. Loss removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of the T-dependent GC response. With repeated OVA+CpG the magnitude of GC formation and the measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced relative to WT+CpG. Most colleagues in this round score this quantitative adjuvant-dependent reduction as “significantly different titre”. Some score it only as a quantitative adjuvant effect and retain SHM competence per se.

Weight of evidence for the question as phrased – titre after repeated OVA+CpG – is loss in G1, G2, G3 and G6, with G4 unchanged and G5 essentially WT-like under the CD4-contact interpretation. That is the G1,G2,G3,G6 set, option B.

Alternative readings that remain in the discussion: 
* strict SHM competence only → MyD88 removed → core AID/CD40/peptide presentation: G1,G2,G3,G5, option D;
* T139A read as peptide-presentation null and MyD88 scored as titre reduction → G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, option C.

Unresolved points: precise functional classification of I-Ad T139A for OVA323-339 presentation vs CD4 binding, and whether CpG-adjuvant magnitude reduction in MyD88-KO is counted as a mechanistic loss of SHM-derived high-affinity titre. Current best synthesis favours option B with the noted caveats.
reflection_text.3:
The high-affinity SHM-derived OVA response is a T-dependent germinal centre/Tfh product requiring enzymatically active AID, CD40–CD40L B-cell licensing for GC/AID induction and OVA peptide presentation on I-Ad to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CD8 co-receptor function is irrelevant for this humoral read-out.

Unambiguous:
* G1 AID-V18R: consensus loss-of-function for SHM/affinity maturation. High-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig essentially absent. Affected.
* G2 CD40-KO: obligatory for Tfh help, GC formation, AID up-regulation, CSR/SHM. Affected.
* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A: peptide-binding groove β1 mutant that abrogates peptide loading/presentation by I-Ad. No OVA peptide presentation to CD4 T cells, no OVA-specific Tfh help, no OVA-specific GC/SHM. Affected.
* G4 CD8-V247D: MHC-I co-receptor defect. CD4/Tfh-dependent humoral response unchanged. Not affected.

Contested:
* G5 H2-IAd-T139A. One view: T139A is a CD4-binding/contact mutant that still allows peptide loading/TCR recognition and with repeated high antigen load Tfh help is retained → WT-like. Opposing view, held by several colleagues and in the OVA/I-Ad literature used here, is that T139A selectively disrupts the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex recognition / peptide presentation of the immunodominant OVA epitope, so OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help and OVA-specific GC/SHM are lost. The question pairs E137A/V142A with T139A as two I-Ad mutants that selectively delete OVA-specific CD4 help. Under the peptide-presentation interpretation G5 is affected; under the CD4-co-receptor interpretation G5 is WT-like.
* G6 MyD88-KO: CpG ODN signals via TLR9–MyD88. Consensus that MyD88 deficiency removes CpG adjuvant-driven DC/B cell licensing and markedly blunts the magnitude of the T-dependent GC response to OVA+CpG. Disagreement is whether this is scored as a loss of SHM per se vs a quantitative adjuvant effect on titre. Strict SHM competence remains, but the titre of high-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig after repeated OVA+CpG immunisation is markedly reduced.

Current weighting: AID, CD40 and I-Ad peptide presentation mutants are unambiguously different from WT. CD8 mutant is unambiguously WT-like. The remaining split is T139A and MyD88.

Most parsimonious exam reading that includes both the selective OVA-specific MHC-II defect T139A and the CpG adjuvant dependence gives G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, i.e. option C. If MyD88 is treated as purely quantitative adjuvant and not a core SHM requirement the set is G1,G2,G3,G5, option D. If T139A is treated as CD4-co-receptor only and not OVA-specific presentation the set with MyD88 included is G1,G2,G3,G6, option B. The discussion remains unresolved on the functional classification of T139A and on whether adjuvant-magnitude reduction counts as “significantly different” titer.
reflection_text.1:
The core T-dependent GC/SHM requirements are stable across rounds.

* High-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig is a germinal centre/Tfh product requiring enzymatically active AID, CD40–CD40L B cell licensing and cognate OVA peptide:I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells.
* G1 AID-V18R is functionally null for SHM/affinity maturation → titer essentially absent.
* G2 CD40-KO abolishes Tfh help, GC formation, AID induction → titer essentially absent.
* G4 CD8-V247D affects MHC-I/CD8 co-receptor. CD8+ CTL function is dispensable for CD4 Tfh-driven GC SHM of a protein antigen → WT-like.

MHC-II I-Ad mutants:

* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A is a peptide-binding groove floor mutation in I-Ad β1 that abrogates peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and abolishes presentation of the immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. OVA-specific Tfh help, GC and SHM are lost. Consensus.
* G5 H2-IAd-T139A is contested. Mechanistic view supported by majority in this round: T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helix at the CD4 co-receptor binding surface, not the peptide floor. T139A impairs CD4–MHC II interaction but leaves peptide binding and TCR recognition of the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex largely intact. Under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG immunisation CD4 co-receptor function can be compensated and OVA-specific Tfh priming/GC SHM remains essentially WT-like. Alternative view held by a minority: T139A is read as destroying the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex and abrogating OVA-specific CD4 priming, so OVA-specific GC/SHM is lost. If that interpretation is taken, G5 behaves like G3.

MyD88:

* G6 MyD88-KO removes TLR9–MyD88 signalling by the CpG adjuvant. CpG drives DC maturation, type I IFN and TLR9 signalling in B cells that amplify the T-dependent GC response to OVA+CpG.
* One camp scores this as a marked quantitative reduction in GC magnitude and therefore a significantly lower titer of high-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig under the OVA+CpG repeated immunisation protocol → G6 different.
* The other camp argues T-dependent GC formation and AID-mediated SHM per se can still occur to protein antigen in the absence of MyD88-dependent TLR signalling; loss is adjuvant magnitude not loss of SHM competence.

Current distribution in round 1:
B. G1,G2,G3,G6 is argued by Colleagues 1,2,4,7,8 with G5 scored WT-like and MyD88 scored as titer-reducing.
C. G1,G2,G3,G5,G6 is argued by Colleagues 3,5,6 with G5 scored as OVA-specific peptide presentation loss and MyD88 scored as titer-reducing.
D. G1,G2,G3,G5 is the strict SHM-competence core without adjuvant magnitude, noted as alternative by several.

Unresolved points: precise classification of T139A in I-Ad as CD4-contact vs peptide-presenting mutant in BALB/c; whether the question intends “significantly different titer” to include quantitative adjuvant amplification via MyD88 or only loss of SHM competence.

Best synthesis retained: AID-V18R, CD40-KO and I-Ad peptide-groove E137A/V142A are unambiguously different; CD8-V247D is a true negative control; T139A is most plausibly a CD4-binding defect compensated under strong repeated immunisation → WT-like; MyD88-KO reduces CpG-adjuvanted magnitude → significantly different titer under the protocol as written. That yields G1,G2,G3,G6, option B, with the noted caveats for G5 and MyD88 scoring.
reflection_text.8:
The high-affinity SHM OVA read-out is a T-dependent germinal centre / Tfh product that requires enzymatically active AID for V-region deamination, CD40–CD40L licensing of B cells for GC entry / AID induction, and productive MHC-II restricted presentation of OVA323-339 on I-Ad to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CD8 co-receptor function is irrelevant for this humoral read-out.

Unanimous:
* G1 AID-V18R – AID catalytic loss → no SHM / affinity maturation → high-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig essentially absent.
* G2 CD40-KO – no CD40 signalling on B cells → no T-dependent GC, no AID induction, no SHM-derived high-affinity OVA Ig.
* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A – E137/V142 are floor residues of the I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. E137A/V142A abrogates peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and abolishes presentation of the immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells → loss of OVA-specific Tfh help, no OVA-specific GC/SHM.
* G4 CD8-V247D – CD8 is an MHC-I co-receptor. MHC-I/CD8 signalling is dispensable for CD4 Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM to a soluble protein. OVA SHM high-affinity titre is essentially WT.

Disagreement persists on G5 H2-IAd-T139A and on the scoring of MyD88.

G5:
* CD4-binding surface view: T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helix at the CD4 co-receptor binding surface. T139A impairs CD4–MHC II engagement but peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained. Under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG prime/boost, CD4 co-receptor function can be compensated and OVA-specific CD4 priming / Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM are retained essentially WT-like. This is the classic distinction with G3 as the peptide-groove mutant.
* Peptide/TCR contact view: T139A selectively destroys recognition / presentation of the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex by OVA-specific CD4+ T cells, i.e. an OVA-specific MHC-II presentation defect, so OVA-specific Tfh help and SHM are lost. Colleagues 3,5,6 take this interpretation.

MyD88:
G6 MyD88-KO removes TLR9→MyD88 signalling of the CpG adjuvant used in the OVA+CpG protocol. The majority view in this round is that MyD88-dependent DC maturation / type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of the T-dependent GC response are required for the magnitude of the response with repeated OVA+CpG immunisation, so the measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced relative to WT+CpG. The alternative strict SHM-competence view treats MyD88 loss as a quantitative adjuvant effect and not a loss of SHM per se.

Integration:
Core T-dependent SHM requirements are G1, G2, G3. G4 is a true negative control. G5 is contested between CD4-binding-compensated WT-like versus OVA-specific presentation null. G6 is generally scored as a significant titre reduction under the OVA+CpG regimen.

Current best reading consistent with the intentional I-Ad mutant pair is E137A/V142A = peptide-binding null G3 defective, T139A = CD4-binding mutant G5 WT-like under strong repeated boosting, and MyD88-KO reduces the CpG-amplified titre. That gives the defective set G1, G2, G3, G6 i.e. option B. If T139A is read as a peptide-presentation null, the set becomes G1,G2,G3,G5,G6 option C, with the strict SHM-only core G1,G2,G3,G5 option D when adjuvant magnitude is excluded. Unresolved is the precise immunological annotation of T139A and whether the adjuvant-dependent quantitative reduction of MyD88-KO is counted as a “significantly different” high-affinity SHM titre.
reflection_text.4:
The high-affinity SHM OVA response is a T-dependent germinal centre/Tfh product requiring enzymatically active AID, CD40–CD40L licensing of B cells, and OVA peptide:I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CpG adjuvant drives magnitude via TLR9–MyD88.

* G1 AID-(V18R): catalytic loss of AID. SHM and affinity maturation abolished. High-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig essentially absent. Unanimously altered.
* G2 CD40-KO: CD40 signalling on B cells obligatory for GC formation, AID induction and Tfh help. No T-dependent GC, no SHM-derived high-affinity OVA Ig. Unanimously altered.
* G3 H2-IAd-(E137A/V142A): E137/V142 are floor residues of the I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. Abrogates peptide binding/loading and presentation of the immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. Loss of OVA-specific Tfh help → no OVA-specific GC/SHM. Unanimously altered.
* G4 CD8-(V247D): MHC-I co-receptor defect. MHC-I/CD8 signalling dispensable for CD4 Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM of a protein T-dependent response. Wild-type like for SHM high-affinity OVA Ig. Unanimous negative control.
* G5 H2-IAd-(T139A): Disagreement persists but mechanising is narrowing.
  - Peptide-presentation/TCR-contact interpretation: T139A destroys I-Ad/OVA323-339 recognition, abrogates OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help → loss of OVA-specific GC/SHM. Argued by Colleagues 3,5,6.
  - CD4-binding/co-receptor interpretation, current majority in round1: T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helical CD4-binding surface. T139A impairs CD4–MHC II interaction but leaves peptide binding and TCR recognition largely intact. Under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG prime/boost CD4 co-receptor function is dispensable for priming of OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells and for GC SHM. OVA-specific high-affinity SHM titre essentially WT-like. Argued by Colleagues 1,2,4,7,8. This matches the classic distinction from the peptide-groove E137A/V142A mutant G3.
* G6 MyD88-KO: CpG ODN signals via TLR9→MyD88 in DCs/B cells. MyD88 deficiency removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of the T-dependent GC response. With the OVA+CpG repeated immunisation protocol the magnitude of GC formation and the measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced relative to WT. Most colleagues now score this as a significant titer difference; a minority scores it as a quantitative adjuvant effect that does not abolish SHM competence per se.

Consensus core: G1, G2, G3 are altered. G4 is not. G5 is contentious; mechanistic CD4-binding interpretation supports WT-like. G6 is scored as significantly reduced in magnitude with the CpG-adjuvanted protocol by the majority in this round.

Hence the most supported set under the OVA+CpG protocol is G1, G2, G3, G6 i.e. option B. If T139A were interpreted as an OVA peptide presentation loss, the altered set would be G1,G2,G3,G5,G6 option C, with the strict SHM-competence core G1,G2,G3,G5 option D. Unresolved is whether the question intends to count the adjuvant-driven quantitative reduction of G6 as a “significantly different” titer versus a qualitative SHM defect.
reflection_text.2:
The high-affinity OVA-specific Ig that is SHM-derived is a T-dependent GC / Tfh output. Non-negotiable requirements are enzymatically competent AID in B cells, CD40–CD40L licensing of B cells for GC entry/AID induction, and cognate OVA peptide : I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CpG ODN adjuvant signals through TLR9–MyD88 and amplifies the magnitude of the T-dependent GC response under the repeated OVA+CpG protocol.

G1 AID-V18R
AID V18R is catalytically dead / SHM-deficient. No V-region deamination, no GC affinity maturation. High-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig is essentially absent. Different from WT. Uncontested.

G2 CD40-KO
CD40 signalling on B cells is obligatory for Tfh help, GC formation, AID up-regulation, class switch and maintenance of the SHM programme. No T-dependent GC → no SHM-derived high-affinity OVA Ig. Different from WT. Uncontested.

G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A
E137/V142 are floor residues of the I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. E137A/V142A abolishes peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and specifically abrogates presentation of the immunodominant BALB/c OVA323-339 epitope to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. Loss of OVA-specific Tfh help → loss of OVA-specific GC and SHM. Different from WT. Uncontested.

G4 CD8-V247D
CD8 is an MHC-I co-receptor. CD8+ CTL function is dispensable for CD4 Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM of a soluble protein T-dependent response. OVA-specific high-affinity SHM Ig titer is essentially WT-like. Uncontested.

G5 H2-IAd-T139A
Disputed mechanistic reading. 
* Peptide-presentation loss reading: T139 lies in the I-Ad β1 helical face contacting the OVA323-339/I-Ad complex; T139A selectively destroys binding/presentation/recognition of the immunodominant OVA peptide by I-Ad while preserving general MHC II expression. OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help is lost → OVA-specific GC/SHM lost. This gives G5 different from WT, as in options C/D.
* CD4-co-receptor contact reading: T139A is the classic I-Ad CD4-binding surface mutant. Peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained; CD4 co-receptor engagement is impaired but dispensable for peripheral T-dependent help under high antigen load and repeated boosting with OVA+CpG. Tfh differentiation and GC SHM to OVA are essentially preserved, so the high-affinity SHM OVA titer is not significantly altered. This gives G5 WT-like, as in options B.
The current round is split ~5 vs 3 on this reading, with the CD4-binding compensated view prevailing among the B-supporters.

G6 MyD88-KO
CpG ODN signals exclusively via TLR9→MyD88 in DCs/B cells. MyD88 deficiency removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated B cell licensing, blunting the adjuvant amplification of the T-dependent GC response. 
* Quantitative titer reading: With repeated OVA+CpG immunisation the magnitude of GC formation and the measurable titer of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced relative to WT+CpG, so the titer is significantly different. This supports inclusion of G6, options B/C.
* Qualitative SHM competence reading: SHM per se can still be generated to protein antigen in the absence of MyD88-dependent TLR signalling; the loss is adjuvant-driven magnitude, not a loss of SHM competence. Under a strict SHM-competence read-out MyD88-KO is not scored as a loss, supporting exclusion of G6, options D and the G1,G2,G3,G5 core.

Consensus core non-negotiable defects: G1, G2, G3. G4 is a true negative control.

Unresolved tension:
* Whether T139A is scored as an OVA-specific peptide-presentation null, G5 different, or a CD4-contact mutant compensated by repeated high-dose OVA+CpG, G5 WT-like.
* Whether a CpG-adjuvant magnitude reduction in MyD88-KO counts as “significantly different” titer of SHM-derived high-affinity antibody, or whether only the qualitative SHM machinery is scored.

The majority current-round positions cluster on B = G1,G2,G3,G6 with CD8-WT and T139A WT-like under repeated boosting, with a sizeable minority on C = G1,G2,G3,G5,G6 and the classical core D = G1,G2,G3,G5 when MyD88 is treated as a quantitative adjuvant effect only.
reflection_text.6:
The high-affinity SHM+ OVA IgG read-out is a T-dependent germinal centre/Tfh product that requires enzymatically active AID, CD40-CD40L licensing of B cells and cognate OVA peptide:I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells for GC entry, AID induction and affinity maturation. CD8 co-receptor function is irrelevant for a MHC-II restricted humoral response.

Uncontroversial core:
* G1 AID-V18R is functionally null for SHM/affinity maturation → high-affinity SHM+ OVA titre essentially absent.
* G2 CD40-KO abolishes Tfh help, GC formation and AID-driven affinity maturation → titre absent.
* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A is a floor of the I-Ad β1 peptide binding groove mutant that abrogates peptide loading/presentation of the BALB/c immunodominant OVA323-339/I-Ad complex → loss of OVA-specific CD4 Tfh help, no OVA-specific GC/SHM → titre absent.
* G4 CD8-V247D impairs MHC-I/CD8 co-receptor function. CD8+ CTL activity is dispensable for CD4 Tfh driven GC SHM of a soluble protein → titre essentially wild type.

Disputed mutants:

H2-IAd-T139A G5. 
Classic immunology literature describes E137A/V142A as the peptide-binding groove null and T139A as the I-Ad β1 helical CD4-co-receptor contact mutant. Under that reading peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained, CD4 engagement is impaired but can be compensated under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG boosting, so OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM remain essentially wild type. Colleagues 1,2,4,7,8 adopt this interpretation and score G5 as WT-like, with Colleague1 noting G5 would join G3 only under a peptide-presentation null reading of T139A.
Colleagues 3,5,6 argue T139 lies in the I-Adβ1 face that contacts the OVA peptide/TCR and T139A selectively destroys presentation/recognition of the immunodominant OVA323-339/I-Ad complex while leaving generic MHC II expression intact, i.e. functionally OVA-specific CD4 help is lost, analogous to G3. That gives the G1,G2,G3,G5 set for the strict SHM competence core.

MyD88-KO G6.
CpG ODN signals via TLR9→MyD88 in DCs/B cells and provides the innate adjuvant drive for the OVA+CpG regimen. MyD88 deficiency removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of the T-dependent GC response. The qualitative SHM programme can still be initiated by protein antigen alone, but the magnitude of GC formation and the measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig after repeated OVA+CpG immunisation is markedly reduced relative to WT+CpG. 
Colleagues 1,2,4,7,8 score this quantitative adjuvant loss as a significant titre difference → G6 included. Colleagues 2,7 note the strict SHM-per-se read-out would treat MyD88 as quantitative only, removing G6 from a purely mechanistic SHM requirement list.

Current balance in round 1: Five colleagues score G1,G2,G3,G6, option B, with G4 WT and G5 WT-like under repeated boosting. Three colleagues score G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, option C, treating T139A as an OVA-specific presentation null and counting the CpG adjuvant effect. The classical AID/CD40/MHC-II core without adjuvant magnitude is G1,G2,G3,G5, option D, and the adjuvant-inclusive presentation-null view is G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, option C.

Unresolved: exact functional classification of I-Ad T139A in BALB/c – CD4-binding/co-receptor contact defect with retained peptide presentation vs selective loss of OVA323-339 presentation – and whether a CpG-driven quantitative reduction of the SHM+ high-affinity titre counts as a “significantly different” titre in the context of an adjuvanted immunisation protocol. CD8-V247D remains a consistent negative control.
reflection_text.7:
The high-affinity SHM OVA response is a T-dependent germinal centre / Tfh product requiring enzymatically competent AID in B cells, CD40–CD40L licensing of B cells by Tfh, and productive OVA peptide : I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CpG ODN adjuvant signals via TLR9–MyD88 and amplifies the magnitude of the OVA+CpG-driven GC response. CD8 co-receptor function is dispensable for an MHC-II restricted humoral response.

Core unequivocal defects:
* G1 AID-(V18R): AID catalytic loss-of-function/SHM-deficient allele. No AID-dependent deamination → no affinity maturation / no high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig. Significantly different from WT.
* G2 CD40-KO: CD40 signalling on B cells obligatory for GC formation, Tfh help maintenance, AID induction, class switch. No T-dependent GC → no SHM-driven high-affinity OVA Ig. Significantly different.
* G3 H2-IAd-(E137A/V142A): E137/V142 are floor residues of the I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. E137A/V142A essentially abolishes peptide binding/loading by I-Ad. OVA323-339 cannot be presented to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells → no OVA-specific Tfh help → no OVA-specific GC/SHM. Significantly different.
* G4 CD8-(V247D): CD8 is an MHC-I co-receptor. MHC-I–CD8 signalling is dispensable for CD4 Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM to a soluble protein antigen. OVA-specific high-affinity SHM Ig essentially WT-like. Not different.

Disputed mutants:
* G5 H2-IAd-(T139A): T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helical face. Majority of current-round colleagues interpret T139A as the classic I-Ad CD4-co-receptor contact mutant. Peptide binding and TCR recognition of the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex are largely retained; CD4 co-receptor engagement is impaired but can be compensated under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG boosting. Hence OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM are largely retained → WT-like for the titre read-out. Minority interpretation treats T139A as selectively destroying OVA peptide presentation/recognition by I-Ad, i.e. functionally analogous to G3, which would make G5 significantly different.
* G6 MyD88-KO: CpG ODN signals exclusively via TLR9→MyD88 in DCs/B cells. MyD88 deficiency removes CpG-driven DC maturation, type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of the T-dependent GC response to the OVA+CpG protocol. The magnitude and measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig after repeated OVA+CpG immunisation is markedly reduced vs WT. Majority scores this as a significant titer difference under the adjuvanted protocol; a strict “SHM competence per se” view would argue SHM qualitatively remains intact and the effect is quantitative/adjuvant dependent.

Current deliberation balance: 5 of 8 colleagues in round 1 now favour G1,G2,G3,G6, Option B, with G4 WT-like and G5 WT-like as a CD4-binding defective mutant compensated by high antigen load. 3 colleagues favour G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, Option C, treating T139A as an OVA-specific peptide presentation loss. Given the majority current reading and the distinction between the peptide-groove mutant G3 and the CD4-contact mutant G5, the most supported set is G1, G2, G3, G6. If T139A is read as an OVA-specific presentation null, the set expands to G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, Option C, with the classical SHM-only core being G1,G2,G3,G5, Option D.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core T-dependent GC/SHM requirements are stable.

* High-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig is a germinal centre/Tfh product requiring enzymatically active AID, CD40–CD40L B cell licensing and cognate OVA323-339:I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CpG ODN provides TLR9–MyD88 innate adjuvant amplification in the OVA+CpG repeated immunisation protocol.

Unambiguous:

* G1 AID-V18R is functionally null for SHM/affinity maturation → titer essentially absent vs WT.
* G2 CD40-KO abolishes Tfh help, GC formation, AID induction → titer essentially absent vs WT.
* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A is a peptide-binding groove floor mutation in I-Ad β1 that abrogates peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and abolishes presentation of the immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. OVA-specific Tfh help, GC and SHM are lost.
* G4 CD8-V247D affects MHC-I/CD8 co-receptor. CD8+ CTL function is dispensable for CD4 Tfh-driven GC SHM of a protein antigen → WT-like. True negative control for humoral immunity.

Contested points:

* G5 H2-IAd-T139A. Mechanistic consensus in round 2: T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helix at the CD4 co-receptor binding surface, not the peptide floor. T139A is the classic I-Ad CD4-binding/co-receptor contact mutant. Peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained; under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG prime/boost CD4 co-receptor engagement can be compensated and OVA-specific Tfh priming/GC SHM remains essentially WT-like. G3 is the peptide-groove null. Minority reading treats T139A as destroying the I-Ad/OVA323-339 complex and abrogating OVA-specific CD4 priming, which would make G5 behave like G3.
* G6 MyD88-KO removes TLR9–MyD88 signalling by CpG adjuvant. Majority in this round scores this as a marked quantitative reduction in GC magnitude and therefore a significantly lower titre of high-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig under the OVA+CpG repeated immunisation protocol → titre significantly different from WT. Minority argues T-dependent GC formation and AID-mediated SHM per se can still occur to protein antigen in absence of MyD88-dependent TLR signalling; loss is adjuvant magnitude not loss of SHM competence.

Current distribution round 2: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 all endorse G1,G2,G3,G6 as the primary set, option B, with explicit caveat noting G5 alternative reading → options C/D if T139A is read as peptide presentation null.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The high-affinity SHM+ OVA IgG read-out after repeated s.c. OVA+CpG is a T-dependent germinal centre/Tfh product in BALB/c requiring enzymatically active AID, CD40–CD40L licensing of B cells and cognate OVA323-339:I-Ad presentation to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh for GC entry, AID induction and affinity maturation. CpG ODN provides TLR9→MyD88 innate adjuvant amplification of magnitude; CD8/MHC-I co-receptor function is irrelevant for this CD4-restricted humoral response.

Stable core across rounds:
* G1 AID-V18R is functionally null for SHM/affinity maturation → high-affinity SHM+ OVA titre essentially absent vs WT.
* G2 CD40-KO abolishes Tfh help, GC formation and AID-driven affinity maturation → titre absent.
* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A is a floor of the I-Ad β1 peptide binding groove mutant that abrogates peptide loading/presentation of the BALB/c immunodominant OVA323-339/I-Ad complex → loss of OVA-specific CD4 Tfh help, no OVA-specific GC/SHM → titre absent.
* G4 CD8-V247D impairs MHC-I/CD8 co-receptor function. CD8+ CTL activity is dispensable for CD4 Tfh-driven GC SHM of a soluble protein → titre essentially wild type. True negative control.

G5 H2-IAd-T139A:
Canonical annotation now dominant in round 3: T139 on the I-Ad β1 helical face contacts CD4, not peptide floor. T139A is the classic I-Ad CD4 co-receptor contact mutant. Peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained. Under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG prime/boost CD4 co-receptor engagement can be compensated and OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM are essentially retained, i.e. WT-like for this T-dependent humoral read-out. G3 is the peptide-groove null. 
Alternative reading held in early rounds and by a minority continues to treat T139A as selectively destroying presentation/recognition of OVA323-339/I-Ad, functionally analogous to G3, which would make G5 defective.

G6 MyD88-KO:
CpG ODN signals via TLR9→MyD88 in DCs/B cells. MyD88 deficiency removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of the T-dependent GC response. Qualitative SHM programme can still be initiated by protein antigen alone, but with the OVA+CpG repeated immunisation protocol the magnitude of GC formation and measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced relative to WT+CpG. Round 3 majority scores this quantitative adjuvant loss as a significantly different titre under the protocol as written. Strict “SHM competence per se” reading would treat MyD88 as quantitative only.

Current balance round 3: 7/8 colleagues converge on G1,G2,G3,G6 different, G4 and G5 WT-like → option B. Caveat preserved: alternative T139A annotation would move G5 into defective set, giving strictly SHM-competence core G1,G2,G3,G5 option D, and with adjuvant magnitude G1,G2,G3,G5,G6 option C. CD8 mutant remains consistent negative control.

Unresolved remains exact in vivo functional classification of I-Ad T139A for OVA323-339 and whether a CpG-driven quantitative reduction counts as “significantly different” vs a qualitative loss of SHM competence. AID/CD40/I-Ad peptide-groove core is settled.

It therefore requires enzymatically active AID in the B cell for V-deamination / affinity maturation, CD40–CD40L licensing for GC entry, AID up-regulation and Tfh maintenance, and cognate presentation of the BALB/c immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope on I-Ad to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh cells. CpG ODN provides TLR9 → MyD88 innate adjuvant amplification of the magnitude of that T-dependent GC response. MHC-I / CD8 co-receptor signalling is dispensable for a soluble protein T-dependent humoral read-out.

* G1 AID-V18R. V18R is catalytically dead for cytidine deamination. V-region SHM and GC affinity maturation are abolished. No high-affinity SHM+ OVA titre. ≠ WT.
* G2 CD40-KO. CD40 signalling on B cells is obligatory for Tfh licensing, GC formation, AID induction and maintenance of the SHM programme. No T-dependent GC → no SHM-derived high-affinity anti-OVA Ig. ≠ WT.
* G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A. E137/V142 are floor residues of the I-Ad β1 peptide binding groove. E137A/V142A abrogates peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and specifically abolishes presentation of OVA323-339 to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. Loss of OVA-specific Tfh help → loss of OVA-specific GC/SHM. ≠ WT.
* G4 CD8-V247D. MHC-I co-receptor defect. CD4 Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM to a T-dependent protein antigen are unchanged. WT-like.
* G5 H2-IAd-T139A. T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helical face that contacts CD4, not the peptide floor. T139A is the classic I-Ad CD4 co-receptor contact mutant. Peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 are largely retained and under repeated high-dose OVA+CpG prime/boost CD4 co-receptor engagement can be compensated. OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help, GC entry and AID-dependent SHM are essentially retained for this T-dependent humoral read-out. WT-like under the protocol used. The peptide-groove null is G3.
* G6 MyD88-KO. CpG ODN signals exclusively via TLR9→MyD88 in DCs/B cells. MyD88 deficiency removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of the T-dependent GC response. With the repeated OVA+CpG regimen the magnitude of GC formation and the measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced vs WT+OVA+CpG.

Hence under the repeated OVA+CpG immunisation the titre of high-affinity SHM+ OVA-specific antibodies is significantly different from WT in G1 AID-V18R, G2 CD40-KO, G3 H2-IAd-E137A/V142A and G6 MyD88-KO. G4 CD8-V247D is a true negative control and G5 I-Ad-T139A is essentially WT-like for this read-out.

That is the G1, G2, G3, G6 set, option B.

Caveat retained as before: on strict qualitative SHM competence the core is G1,G2,G3, and if T139A were read as an OVA-specific peptide/TCR contact loss rather than the canonical CD4-binding defect G5 would join, giving the D/C alternatives. On canonical annotation T139A is a CD4-contact mutant compensated by repeated boosting.

* G4 CD8-V247D: MHC-I co-receptor defect. CD4 Tfh help, GC formation and AID-dependent SHM to a soluble T-dependent antigen are unchanged. OVA-specific high-affinity SHM Ig is WT-like. = WT
* G5 H2-IAd-T139A: T139 lies on the I-Ad β1 helical face that contacts CD4, not the peptide floor. T139A is the canonical I-Ad CD4 co-receptor contact mutant. 5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: High-affinity SHM+ OVA-specific Ig after repeated s.c. OVA+CpG in BALB/c is a CD4+ Tfh-dependent germinal centre output. Core requirements are enzymatically active AID for V-region deamination, CD40–CD40L licensing for GC entry/AID induction/Tfh maintenance, and cognate presentation of the BALB/c immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope on I-Ad to OVA-specific CD4+ Tfh. CpG ODN provides TLR9→MyD88 innate adjuvant amplification of the magnitude of that T-dependent GC response; MHC-I/CD8 co-receptor function is dispensable for this humoral read-out.

G1 AID-(V18R): catalytically dead AID. V-region SHM and GC affinity maturation abolished. High-affinity SHM+ OVA Ig essentially absent vs WT. Unanimous loss.

G2 CD40-KO: obligatory for Tfh licensing, GC formation, AID up-regulation, class switch and maintenance of SHM programme. No T-dependent GC, no SHM-derived high-affinity anti-OVA Ig. Unanimous loss.

G3 H2-IAd-(E137A/V142A): E137/V142 are floor residues of I-Ad β1 peptide-binding groove. Abrogates peptide binding/loading of I-Ad and specifically abolishes presentation of OVA323-339. No OVA-specific CD4 priming/Tfh help → no OVA-specific GC/SHM. Unanimous loss.

G4 CD8-(V247D): MHC-I co-receptor defect. CD4 Tfh help/GC/SHM to soluble protein unaffected. Unanimous WT-like.

G5 H2-IAd-(T139A): canonical annotation is I-Ad β1 CD4 co-receptor contact mutant, not peptide-groove null. Peptide binding and TCR recognition of I-Ad/OVA323-339 largely retained; CD4 engagement impaired but compensable under high antigen load/repeated OVA+CpG boosting, so OVA-specific Tfh help and GC SHM essentially preserved, WT-like for this T-dependent humoral read-out. The peptide-groove null is G3. Minority reading treats T139A as selective loss of OVA323-339 presentation/recognition, i.e. an OVA-specific CD4 help defect analogous to G3.

G6 MyD88-KO: CpG signals exclusively via TLR9-MyD88. Loss removes CpG-driven DC maturation/type I IFN and TLR9-mediated amplification of T-dependent GC response. With repeated OVA+CpG the magnitude of GC formation and measurable titre of high-affinity SHM-derived anti-OVA Ig is markedly reduced relative to WT+CpG. Most colleagues now score this adjuvant-dependent quantitative reduction as “significantly different titre” under the protocol as written, even though qualitative SHM programme per se remains competent.

Current round convergence: 8/8 colleagues present B = G1,G2,G3,G6 as primary answer, with explicit caveats. Disputed points remain:
* Functional classification of I-Ad T139A: CD4-binding/co-receptor defect with largely retained peptide presentation vs OVA-specific peptide presentation/TCR contact null. Literature support favours CD4-contact interpretation, E137A/V142A is peptide-groove null.
* Whether CpG-adjuvant magnitude reduction in MyD88-KO is counted as mechanistic loss of SHM-derived high-affinity titre. Protocol uses OVA+CpG, so titre is significantly different.

Alternative mappings discussed: strict SHM competence only → G1,G2,G3,G5, option D; T139A read as peptide-presentation null plus MyD88 magnitude → G1,G2,G3,G5,G6, option C.
